title: Correlate Storyboard — Filter Composer & Session Bookmarks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design a storyboard-style request drilldown panel that surfaces correlated session lanes, ad-hoc filter composition, and persistent session bookmarks. The goal is to make deep-dive debugging faster for engineers by: 1) visually grouping related requests by correlation IDs and inferred causality, 2) letting users compose reusable filter expressions via a compact composer, and 3) enabling one-click bookmark snapshots that pin the current filter + span selection to a rollout or cost-analysis card. This ticket covers the low-fidelity flows, an interactive prototype for usability testing, and a handover spec for engineering implementation of the composer and bookmark annotation layers.
acceptance_criteria: Storyboard panel shows at least three correlated lanes for a selected request with clear correlation-id badges
Filter composer supports and/or/not operators, saves named filters, and exposes quick-presets (latency, error, cold-start)
Bookmarks can be created from the panel and referenced in Rollouts and Cost view cards
Prototype validated with 5 engineers/SEs and top 3 usability issues addressed
Handover artifact includes accessibility notes and CSS spec for compact lanes
design_decisions: Use horizontal lanes (storyboard) instead of stacked timeline to emphasize causal threads — trade-off: reduced precise timing resolution but improved mental model for correlated requests
Compact badges for correlation IDs to avoid overwhelming header space; full ID displayed on hover — trade-off: extra hover step for exact ID copy

Filter composer is expression-first (text) with tokenized suggestions rather than modal dropdowns to scale for power users — trade-off: slightly higher discoverability cost mitigated by presets and inline tips

Filter composer text-entry was fastest for power users; newcomers preferred the token suggestions — add inline examples
Bookmarks were conceptually useful but needed metadata (timestamp, creator, linked rollout) to be discoverable
Copy ID behavior: users expected single-click copy — changed from hover to click with toast confirmation
